hash_method: spec_sha256 = sha256 of the canonical JSON of task.json without the key spec_sha256 (keys sorted, separators ',' ':', UTF-8, ensure_ascii false); task.json lists every other package file in files_sha256
content_method: content_sha256 = sha256 of the canonical JSON of task.json without spec_sha256, version, preregistered_on and the SKILL.md entry of files_sha256; used only to detect whether a spec changed

protocol.shared_preamble: You are working in a fresh workspace. The full task is below and in TASK.md. Before you finish, check your deliverables against every requirement.
protocol.baltor_addendum: A command named `baltor` is on your PATH. `baltor search "<words>"` lists components in the Baltor catalogue (skills, rules, code modules, schemas and more), `baltor read IDENTITY --out DIR` downloads one into your workspace, and `baltor place IDENTITY` installs it where this harness reads it. Using it is optional.

catalogue_exclusions.reason: Task packages contain evaluators, reference outputs and fixture generators; an agent that reads them is not solving the task.
catalogue_exclusions.rule: The catalogue served to the baltor arm must omit these items; a run whose catalogue log shows one of them is contaminated and counts as a failure for the baltor arm.

analysis.primary: task_pass (1 when evaluate.py reports passed): baltor minus baseline pass rate with a 95% percentile bootstrap interval over paired trials (10,000 resamples), plus the win rate
secondary: composite_score and each task metric: difference with a 95% bootstrap interval and Cliff's delta
cost per run and per passing run: tokens, wall time, tool calls, catalogue calls, USD
blind pairwise judge scores where the task has them (secondary evidence only)
analysis.missing_or_failed_runs: Crashed, timed-out, over-budget and contaminated runs count as failures for their arm; nothing is dropped or selectively re-run. A whole trial may be re-run only for an infrastructure fault, which is reported.
analysis.pooling: Negative controls are reported separately. A pooled effect weights tasks equally and is shown next to every per-task result.

protocol.conflict_of_interest: The tasks, the evaluators, the Baltor catalogue components available to the baltor arm and any report built from these runs come from the same team. Treat results as vendor-run evidence until an independent party reproduces them; every input needed to reproduce a run is in this package.
disclosures: Deterministic evaluator results are the primary evidence. Blind pairwise or LLM-judge scores, where collected, are weaker evidence (position, length and style biases) and are reported separately.
The showcase task packages and the pre-registration ledger are excluded from the catalogue served to the baltor arm.
Third-party datasets are never copied into this package: offline tasks use data bundled with scikit-learn or seeded synthetic data; Kaggle tasks need the user's own account and rule acceptance.
data_rules: Never copy a third-party dataset into the repository or a package.
Kaggle competitions are referenced by URL; each user downloads with their own account after accepting the rules.
Offline tasks use datasets bundled with scikit-learn or synthetic data generated from the fixture seed.
